result: The authors screened alternative amino acids at the proline position in the Connectase recognition sequence and found that substitutions with S, C, and A resulted in moderate or high ligation rates, while most other amino acids drastically reduced ligation rates. They conclude that amino acids possessing a β-carbon but lacking a γ-carbon can be used in this position.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm this finding. One reviewer states the author 'is able to make this process irreversible by screening different Connectase recognition sites to find an alternative sequence that is also accepted by the enzyme.' Another reviewer notes 'The author optimized the protocol's efficiency with assays replacing a single amino acid.' The data in Figure 2 is accepted without challenge.

result: The authors demonstrate that BcPAP can be produced in E. coli and used to shift the Connectase reaction equilibrium, achieving 98-100% conversion of the less abundant substrate in protein-protein and protein-peptide ligations without side products. The method works at various substrate concentrations (10-100 µM) and temperatures (10-22°C), with reaction rates varying accordingly but still achieving complete fusions.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly support these findings. One reviewer states 'The author provides convincing evidence that an alternative to traditional protein fusion synthesis is more efficient with 100% yields using connectase' and notes 'identification of a proline aminopeptidase, Bacilius coagulans (BcPAP), as a usable enzyme to use in the fusion reaction.' The editor describes 'compelling well-controlled data showing the technique works for various protein partners.'

result: LC-MS analysis of a 1:1 Ub-MBP conjugation showed 99.6% fusion product with minimal unconjugated substrates (0.25% Ub, 0.13% MBP). The N-terminal proline was almost completely (99.8%) removed from the peptide byproduct, supporting that BcPAP acts exclusively on N-terminal proline residues.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this data without challenge. One reviewer notes 'proteomic mass spec confirmation revealed fusion products were achieved' and describes the work as having 'convincing evidence.' The thorough characterization by LC-MS is implicitly accepted as part of the 'well-controlled data.'

result: The authors show that Connectase is unaffected by protease inhibitors, while the equilibrium shift associated with BcPAP activity could be suppressed with serine protease inhibitors PMSF and AEBSF, consistent with BcPAP's classification as a serine protease.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge this characterization. The data is presented in Appendix 1—figure 4 and accepted as part of the overall method validation. One reviewer notes the 'thorough study' warrants publication, implicitly accepting these mechanistic details.

result: The authors demonstrate antibody conjugation by transfecting HEK293 cells with αHER2 antibody constructs and achieving near-complete labeling (97-98% efficiency) with either peptides or ubiquitin. SDS-PAGE and LC-MS analysis showed that HC2 and HC2LC1 assemblies were completely conjugated, while HC2LC2 was predominantly conjugated to four molecules (83% for peptide, 95% for ubiquitin). The conjugation products remained stable in blood plasma for several days.
evaluation: Reviewers strongly support this result. One reviewer states 'Multiple examples including Ubiquitin, GST, and antibody fusion/conjugations reveal how this method can be applied to a diverse range of biological processes.' The editor notes this work 'will also be of interest to those studying fusion oncoproteins' and describes 'compelling well-controlled data.' The antibody conjugation data is central to demonstrating the method's utility.

result: The authors demonstrate protein cyclization using ubiquitin at different concentrations. At 10 µM, circular assemblies of predominantly Ub-C2 (80%) and Ub-C3 (20%) were formed, while at 100 µM, larger circular assemblies were produced (37% Ub-C2, 45% Ub-C3, 9% Ub-C4, 6% Ub-C5, 2% Ub-C6). Single ubiquitin molecules were not efficiently circularized, suggesting the N- and C-termini are too far apart without additional linker sequences. The yields of specific assemblies can be controlled by modifying reaction conditions and substrate design.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this demonstration without challenge. One reviewer notes 'Multiple examples including Ubiquitin, GST, and antibody fusion/conjugations reveal how this method can be applied to a diverse range of biological processes.' The cyclization/polymerization data is treated as a valid application of the method.

result: The authors present a method that reliably obtains 100% fusion product in 1:1 conjugation reactions by altering the Connectase recognition sequence so the peptide byproduct can be specifically inactivated by BcPAP. The method is efficient for protein-protein and protein-peptide fusions at N- or C-termini, enables generation of defined and completely labeled antibody conjugates, requires short incubation times with small amounts of enzyme, and is effective at low substrate concentrations and temperatures.
evaluation: Reviewers strongly support the overall method. One reviewer states 'this novel enzymatic protein fusion method has several applications in the field of bioconjugation' and 'provides a novel, reproducible way to enzymatically create protein-protein conjugates.' The editor describes it as 'a versatile addition to the chemical protein modifications and bioconjugation toolbox' with 'compelling well-controlled data.' Another reviewer notes 'The thorough study and efficiency of the method...warrants publication.'

result: The authors acknowledge that the main disadvantage of Connectase is its relatively long recognition sequence (13 amino acids N-terminal, 19 amino acids C-terminal), resulting in a final conjugation 'scar' of 19-25 amino acids. This is comparable to SpyTag/KTag but longer than Sortase-mediated fusions. Long linker sequences can potentially interfere with protein folding, be susceptible to proteases, or be immunogenic, though these problems have not been encountered for Connectase so far. The method is primarily useful where this longer scar can be tolerated.
evaluation: One reviewer explicitly raises this as a significant concern: 'Though the ~100% ligation efficiency is an advancement, the long recognition linker may be the biggest drawback. For large native proteins...the multiple interruptions with long linkers will likely interfere with protein folding, resulting in non-native protein structures.' The reviewer concludes the method is 'limited to generating epitope/peptide/protein tagged proteins, and not for synthetic protein biology aimed at examining native/endogenous protein function in vitro.' This represents a substantive limitation that tempers the method's applicability.

result: The authors claim Connectase offers greater substrate specificity, higher catalytic efficiency, catalyzes no side reactions compared to other protein ligases, and acts on a longer recognition sequence leading to these advantages.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these comparative advantages. One reviewer notes 'Connectase specifically can provide some benefits over the more widely used Sortase, depending on the nature of the species that is desired to be conjugated.' The absence of side reactions is confirmed by the data showing no side products in Figures 3A-C. The editor describes the technology as 'cleverly uses Connectase to irreversibly fuse proteins.'

result: The authors describe methodological approaches to prevent N-terminal acetylation: using TEV protease cleavage of precursors or adding an extra N-terminal proline that is removed by BcPAP during the reaction. TEV cleavage and conjugation can be performed in parallel with small amounts of enzyme.
evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these methodological details. The approaches are presented as practical solutions and are accepted as part of the overall method validation. The data in Figure 3F and Appendix 1—figure 2B support these claims without reviewer objection.
